conceptZh: 根是長在土裡、撐住植物的部分
object: a tiny felt ninja and a bouncy acorn that ricochets around the frame
morph: a bouncing acorn ricochets off the floor, walls and the ninja's head and each hit knocks one stroke of 根 into place
creativeAngle: 布忍者躲在盆栽後以為沒人看見，橡實彈來彈去，每撞一次就落下一筆；詞用「樹根」。
promptEn: An 8-second 3D animated toy clip on a clean solid pale sky-white backdrop, locked camera. The only text is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 根, centered in saturated chestnut-brown strokes about 70 percent of frame height, with the wood radical 木 on the left and the 艮 part on the right. Cast: Fumi, a tiny felt ninja in a dark-teal hood with stitched eyes who is spectacularly bad at hiding and is convinced no one can see him, and a bouncy round brown acorn with a little cap. Moment one, 0 to 1.7s: Fumi tiptoes in and flattens himself behind a thin blade of grass, his whole body plainly visible, while an acorn drops from above and bounces off the floor with a squeak. The first 根 is spoken as the acorn hits the ground, and the vertical stroke of 木 shoots up from the point of impact. Moment two, 1.7 to 3.4s: the acorn ricochets off the left edge of the frame, whacks Fumi on the head with a soft thump, and he freezes in a pose, pretending to be a leaf. The second 根 is spoken as the acorn's next bounce lands the crossing bar and two slanting strokes of 木. Moment three, 3.4 to 5.0s: the acorn caroms off the right edge and rolls in a zigzag, each bump dropping one stroke of 艮 into place on the right side, with the little square and the long crossing strokes landing one by one, while Fumi dives left and right, still convinced he is hidden. The acorn finally rolls into Fumi's arms and he hugs it, startled. Moment four, 5.0s onward: Fumi plants the acorn in a pot at the bottom edge and a tiny sprout pops out; he bows. From 5.0 to 8.0s the glyph is perfectly still and uncovered while Fumi, delighted, tiptoes in a tiny circle around the potted sprout, ninja-bowing to it, never touching the strokes. Audio: a warm friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin says exactly 「根、根、樹根」, slowly with clear tones as ㄍㄣ、ㄍㄣ、ㄕㄨˋ ㄍㄣ. First 根 near 0.7s, second near 2.4s, and 樹根 around 5.3s as the sprout pops up. Stop after the word. Only soft squeaks and thumps, no background music. Soft studio lighting, vivid not neon colors, no flashing, no lens flare, no watermark, no subtitles, no vocabulary text, and no writing other than the single glyph 根.

conceptZh: 積木小隊想抓坐在大樹幹上的調皮小老鼠，先疊高塔摔倒，再排成衝撞隊用力撞樹幹，撞得積木四散落下排成「根」，樹幹底下的樹根也彈出來。
object: a squad of chunky interlocking toy building bricks in chestnut-brown, led by a brick with two googly eyes and a tiny flag, plus a big chunky toy tree trunk at the right edge with a cheeky cartoon mouse perched on top
morph: the squad charges the tree trunk as a battering ram; the BONK scatters the bricks upward and they drop into place as the strokes of 根, the 木 bricks on the left and the 艮 bricks on the right, while the trunk's roots burst out of the floor for the spoken word 樹根
creativeAngle: 上一版是布忍者和橡果的彈跳，這次改成積木小隊的「衝撞」模式：積木本身就是筆畫材料，撞樹幹後四散落下自然排成「根」，而樹幹底下彈出的樹根正好對應念出的詞「樹根」，聽到的和看到的是同一個故事。小老鼠只當挑釁目標，畫面上只有三樣東西，保持乾淨。
promptEn:
An 8-second 3D animated toy clip on a clean solid pale cream backdrop, locked camera, soft studio lighting. The only text is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 根, built from chestnut-brown toy bricks, centered, about 70 percent of frame height, with the wood radical 木 on the left and 艮 on the right. Cast: the Brick Squad, eight chunky interlocking brown toy bricks led by Captain Brick, a brick with googly eyes and a tiny paper flag, bossy and overconfident; a big chunky toy tree trunk standing at the right edge of the frame; and one tiny cheeky cartoon mouse with big round ears sitting on top of the trunk, grinning and twirling an acorn.

0 to 1.5s: the squad marches in from the left in a neat line, click-click-click. Captain Brick spots the mouse, stops dead, and points his flag at it. The mouse waves the acorn and sticks out its tongue.

1.5 to 3.0s: first try. The bricks hop on top of each other into a tall wobbly tower, Captain Brick on top stretching toward the mouse. The tower sways, leans, and topples flat with a soft clatter, bricks everywhere. The mouse hops in place, delighted.

3.0 to 4.3s: the squad snaps together into one long battering ram, Captain Brick at the nose. They dig in, lean way back in a big visible wind-up, freeze for a beat, then charge across the frame at full speed with a rising whir.

4.3 to 5.0s: BONK. The ram squashes flat against the trunk, the trunk shudders, the mouse pops up and lands on its tail. The crash shakes all the bricks loose: they fly upward in a brown fountain and drop neatly into place as the glyph 根 in the center, first the tall vertical, crossbar and two slanting strokes of 木 on the left, then the strokes of 艮 on the right, clicking together one by one.

5.0 to 8.0s: the finished 根 holds perfectly still and uncovered. Just below the trunk, in the bottom right corner, tangled toy roots burst out of the floor and wiggle, and the mouse rides one root like a tiny wave. Captain Brick, flattened like a pancake, wobbles upright in the bottom left corner with a dizzy grin and spinning googly eyes, then does a proud little salute with his bent flag, never touching the strokes.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin says exactly 「根、根、樹根」, read slowly and distinctly with clear tones as ㄍㄣ、ㄍㄣ、ㄕㄨˋ ㄍㄣ. First 根 near 1.6s as the bricks start stacking, second 根 near 4.5s as the scattered bricks click into the glyph, and 樹根 near 5.4s exactly as the roots burst out beneath the trunk. Stop after the word. Only soft clicks, a squashy bonk and a tiny squeak, no background music. Bright but not neon colors, no flashing, no lens flare, no watermark, no subtitles, no vocabulary text, and no writing other than the single glyph 根.
